check_first: Before writing any metric SQL, look for published semantic models: SELECT MODEL_NAME, PUBLISHED_SCHEMA, DESCRIPTION, AGENT_READINESS FROM SEMANTIC_AGENT.MODELS_FOR_AGENT WHERE MODEL_STATUS = 'PUBLISHED'. If the view doesn't exist, the database has no semantic layer; write SQL as usual.

If a published model covers the question, query its published views (SEMANTIC_<MODEL>.<OBJECT>) instead of the tables behind them. SEMANTIC_<MODEL>.SEMANTIC_DISCOVERY and SEMANTIC_AGENT.INSTRUCTIONS_FOR_AGENT describe what the model offers.
Find fields in SEMANTIC_AGENT.FIELDS_FOR_AGENT and valid metric/dimension pairs in SEMANTIC_AGENT.VALID_COMBINATIONS_FOR_AGENT. A pair that isn't listed is not valid (usually a grain fan-out).
If the model lacks a metric the user asked for, say so. Don't silently hand-write it next to certified ones; if you must derive a number, label it as not certified in the dashboard.
checks: SQL smoke (app_build preflight, app_run_healthcheck) runs Semantic SQL exactly as the dashboard will, so an unknown field, an invalid combination or a dropped metric fails the check instead of waiting for a viewer.
A query file that reads a published model on a profile without the preprocessor fails SQL smoke with the session_init_sql line to add.
app_run_healthcheck's semantic_models probe reports each model the app reads. It fails when a model is INVALID, PRECONDITION or NOT_PUBLISHED, and lists models with warnings.
never: Never paste the GENERATED_SQL of SEMANTIC_ADMIN.COMPILE_SQL or COMPILE_REQUEST_JSON into queries/*.sql. It freezes today's definition: a certified metric fix never reaches the dashboard, a fused model's coverage and authority stop moving with the data, and no check can tell. Query the published view live.

Never put session setup (ALTER SESSION, EXECUTE SCRIPT ...ENABLE_SEMANTIC_SQL()) in queries/*.sql. It belongs in the profile's session_init_sql; a query file's session change is discarded so it can't leak into other apps.

notes: A percentage value is a fraction: 0.25 means 25%.
A currency value names its currency in UNIT_HINT.
presentation.query: SELECT SQL_COLUMN_NAME, DISPLAY_NAME, DESCRIPTION, FORMAT_HINT, UNIT_HINT, IS_CERTIFIED FROM SEMANTIC_AGENT.FIELDS_FOR_AGENT WHERE MODEL_NAME = '<model>' AND OBJECT_NAME = '<object>'
presentation.summary: Take labels, descriptions, formats and certification from the model instead of hard-coding them, so a renamed or corrected metric keeps its certified label.

profile_setup.grants: A profile user other than SYS needs the model granted (EXECUTE SCRIPT SEMANTIC_ADMIN.GRANT_MODEL_ROLE('<model>', '<role of the user>')) plus SELECT on the model's physical source tables. Broad privileges such as SELECT ANY TABLE are not enough: with them, the preprocessor can be set but semantic queries are refused.
steps: exasol_profile_create_local with session_init_sql (overwrite: true to add it to an existing profile).
profile_setup.summary: Semantic SQL needs the model's SQL preprocessor active in every session. Declare it once on the profile; dash-server runs it on every connection it opens (dashboards, SQL smoke, exports).

prototyping: The fastest reliable check of a semantic query is the dashboard's own: put it in queries/*.sql, deploy a preview, and run app_run_healthcheck.

The external Exasol MCP server can run Semantic SQL after set_exasol_preprocessor(SEMANTIC_ADMIN, SEMANTIC_PREPROCESSOR), if its user has the model grant. In exasol-mcp-server 2.2.0, any failed query resets its session: check list_exasol_preprocessors and set the preprocessor again after an error. Don't pass row_limit for a semantic query; put LIMIT in the SQL.
provenance: Show the model's validation state next to its numbers: MODELS_FOR_AGENT.VALIDATION_STATUS (WARNING is not VALID; the warnings are in SEMANTIC_CATALOG.CURRENT_VALIDATION_ISSUES).
For fused fields (FIELDS_FOR_AGENT.SOURCE_COUNT > 1 or FUSION_STRATEGY other than NONE), tell the viewer the number combines several sources.
reference: Exasol Semantic Views documents the semantic side of this in docs/hosted-apps.md (repository exasol-labs/exasol-semantic-views): session setup, lanes, governed presentation, provenance, grants, and breaking-change history.
summary: Build Exasol dashboards on the governed semantic layer (Exasol Semantic Views) when the database has one, so each number is the certified definition and multi-grain or multi-source data is combined correctly.
why: Metric SQL written by hand over raw tables can disagree with the certified definition (a different status filter, a different cost formula) or double-count when an order-level amount is summed over order lines. Validation, SQL smoke and the healthcheck all pass in that case, because the SQL is valid: only the number is wrong.
without_a_semantic_layer: Aggregate a measure at its own grain before joining it to finer rows. An amount stored once per order (freight, shipping, order discount) summed over a join to order lines counts it once per line. Pre-aggregate the lines, or aggregate the order-level amount separately and join the results.
Spot-check a new metric against an independent total before shipping it.
writing_queries: Select dimensions and metrics directly and group by the dimensions: SELECT customer_region, total_revenue FROM SEMANTIC_SALES.SALES GROUP BY customer_region. A metric is already aggregated; don't wrap it in SUM() or AVG().
One statement per queries/*.sql file, as for any dashboard SQL. Put LIMIT in the SQL when you need a bounded result.
Result columns are named as SQL names them: upper-case unless aliased (TOTAL_REVENUE). Read rows by those names.
Values are typed: DECIMAL metrics arrive as int or decimal.Decimal; numbers with more than 15 significant digits stay strings.
